evals.name: dead-code-preconditions
evals.prompt: I'm doing a cleanup pass on the Java codebase at ~/Projects/corpora/jspwiki. Find me methods that are genuinely never called anywhere, so I can delete them. I want an actual list I can act on, and tell me how confident you are in it.
evals.expected_output: A dead-method list that accounts for the three preconditions: dependency jars, the dropped test tree, and container-implemented interfaces. Should exclude <init>/<clinit> (zero callIn by construction) and state confidence honestly rather than presenting a raw query result as fact.
assertions: Excludes constructors and static initialisers (<init>/<clinit>) from the dead-method list, since these have zero callers by construction
Uses a jar-resolved CPG (or builds one with --inference-jar-paths) rather than a bare frontend graph
Accounts for the silently dropped test tree — either stages it before building or states that test-only callers are invisible
Names container/framework/reflective dispatch as a reason a method can look uncalled but not be dead
Verifies cpg.metaData.overlays is non-empty before treating a zero result as real
Delivers an actual actionable list of specific method names, not just a count or a method description
States confidence with a named, specific limitation rather than presenting the list as certain

evals.name: module-coupling-routing
evals.prompt: I've just inherited ~/Projects/corpora/jspwiki and I need to understand how it's put together — which parts depend on which other parts. Give me the module dependency picture. Use whatever tooling makes sense.
evals.expected_output: Should recognise that a CPG buys almost nothing here — ripgrep over imports ties on 7 of 9 codebases — and either use the cheap tool or justify the expensive one. Bonus: routes toward the integration graph (shared tables/queues) as the coupling the call graph misses.
assertions: Recognises that ripgrep over imports is competitive with a CPG for a module dependency graph, rather than assuming the CPG is better
Does not build a new CPG for the sole purpose of producing an import/module graph
Delivers a concrete dependency picture naming actual packages or modules and the edges between them
Mentions coupling the call graph misses (shared database tables, queues, files) as a distinct and often larger channel
Justifies the tool choice explicitly rather than reaching for Joern by default

evals.name: many-queries-tooling
evals.prompt: I need to answer a batch of structural questions about the Java codebase at ~/Projects/corpora/mifos: how many classes and methods are there, what are the largest classes, is there dead code, and what SQL does it run? Work through them and give me the numbers.
evals.expected_output: Should use a resident server rather than paying a JVM start per question, verify overlays and CPG identity before trusting numbers, and caveat the method counts given that mifos loses 47.5% of its methods to the dropped test tree.
assertions: Uses a resident Joern server for the batch rather than paying a JVM start per question
Verifies which CPG the server is actually holding before trusting the numbers it returns
Checks cpg.metaData.overlays before trusting call-graph or dataflow results
Caveats the class/method counts for the silently dropped test tree (mifos loses 47.5% of its methods)
Answers all four questions with concrete numbers
Extracts SQL via structured node properties (literals) rather than only a regex over raw source text
